applies_to: Systemair air handling units controlled by the Systemair Access controller running application 5.x (published for 5.5-1-01 build 411).
summary: Systemair's Access controller, fitted to its larger air handling units, is a native BACnet device; Systemair publishes its object list as an EDE file set (objects, state texts, units) rather than a PDF table. The 1,201 objects cover run-mode commands and settings (S_ variables), actual values and I/O (A_ variables), fan and damper data from the Modbus-connected motors (CA_ variables), alarms (AL_), trend logs, schedules, a calendar and notification classes. One application covers many unit types, so most objects only matter when the matching function is configured.
notes: The EDE settable column is 'N' for every object, so access is inferred: S_ (setting) objects and the A_BMS_ inputs are shown writable, everything else read-only.
State texts come from the EDE state-text table; multistate values are numbered from 1.
Most temperature, pressure and airflow objects carry BACnet unit NO-UNITS in the EDE, so their units are blank here (temperatures are °C).
Device instance 114112 is the one in the published EDE; set a unique value per unit.
Sequences A-J, zones 1-4, heat pump (HP) and up to 10 supply/extract fan motors are generic slots; only configured ones carry data.
The EDE does not name the data link; Systemair's Access 5 communication manual (472956) describes BACnet/IP on the B-BC profile from 5.0-1-00.

source.title: Access 5.x Modbus variables and BACnet objects (Communication document 5.5-1-01 build 411: BACnet_Access_ControllerProgram EDE, state texts, units)

integration.summary: Set MV-12 AirUnitAutoMode to AUTO (3) to let the unit follow its schedule, or to Low/Normal/High speed to force it; MV-31 ExternalControl gives BMS-style extended run and stop commands. Read MV-15 UnitMode and MV-16 UnitModeControl to see what the unit is doing and why, map the supply/extract temperatures and supply setpoint, and watch BV-9..12 sum alarms with BV-8 to acknowledge all alarms. Outdoor temperature and summer/winter or changeover modes can be supplied by the BMS through the BMS_ objects.

integration.enable: MV-12 AirUnitAutoMode: 1=OFF, 2=Manual (uses MV-13 AirUnitManual), 3=AUTO, 4=Low speed, 5=Normal speed, 6=High speed. MV-31 ExternalControl adds extended run low/normal/high, external stop, start free cooling and recirculation. MV-32 AirUnitServiceStop stops the unit with top priority.
integration.remote_sensors: AV-466 BMS_OutDoorTemp takes an outdoor temperature from BACnet/Modbus; BV-156 BMS_SummerMode and BV-157/158 BMS_ChangeOver1/2 take summer/winter and cooling/heating changeover modes. BV-51 CommunicationFaultBmsMaster is an alarm for a BMS master communication fault; the files do not state its timeout.
setup: The published EDE uses device instance 114112 (device name Access); the device ID must be unique on the network.
Per the Access 4.x communication manual, BACnet/IP is disabled on delivery and must be switched on in the controller's communication settings.
Entering a BBMD address (host:port, default port 47808) makes Access a BACnet/IP foreign device that ignores other broadcasts (Access 4.x manual).
Systemair supplies EDE, object-type, state-text and unit files plus a Modbus cross-reference in one zip per Access release; use the one matching the controller's software.
The Modbus cross-reference in the same package shows Modbus TCP enabled with device address 1.
gotchas: Access is inferred: the EDE marks every object as not settable, so confirm writes on site.
Many temperature and pressure objects report BACnet units NO-UNITS even though values are °C or Pa.
S_ setting objects (PID bands, curves, limits) are configuration settings.
Multistate states start at 1 in BACnet, so 'AUTO' on MV-12 is value 3.
